rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because a divine day can equal one thousand or, sometimes, fifty thousand earthly days, Islahi reads creation days as phases.
rows.anchor: For this reason, the word “day” should be interpreted to mean “phases.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other Qur'anic passages give a six-day creation; this passage details that span and says the earth itself was created in two days.
rows.anchor: Here, details of this overall span are mentioned as to how much days were spent in the creation of the components.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone created the earth and is therefore its Lord; Arab idolaters acknowledged Him as Creator of everything yet still assigned Him partners, for which they were reprimanded.
rows.anchor: the idolaters set up partners and associates with Him. Even though He Who created the earth is also its Lord

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mountains stabilize the earth so it does not tumble with its creatures; Islahi connects this purpose to 32:10.
rows.anchor: the wisdom behind this was to maintain the earth’s balance lest it may have tumbled away with all its creatures.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mountains are visible signs of God's power on the earth's surface; Islahi links this appeal to the observations in 88:17–20.
rows.anchor: attention is directed to the mountains with reference to this very aspect in the following words:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording about blessing the earth and measuring its provisions means that God placed benefits, blessings, and all kinds of sustenance there.
rows.anchor: God placed various benefits and blessings within the earth and also placed in it all types of sustenance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth's blessings appear in abundant vegetation and multiplied yields: one seed can produce hundreds, and a planting can benefit descendants for generations.
rows.anchor: man sows one seed and the earth gives him several hundred seeds in return as its produce.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scientific inquiry may exhaust its tools, but the earth's hidden treasures will not run out.
rows.anchor: the treasures of this earth will never diminish.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God provides sustenance in proportion to the creatures on earth, entrusting their provisions to the earth and guiding people in how to extract them.
rows.anchor: the Almighty has consigned to the earth’s custody the sustenance of every creature created by Him, and has also guided man how to extract it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four days are the total time for creating the earth, setting its mountains, and placing provisions in it.
rows.anchor: the time taken to create the earth and setting forth mountains on it and placing provisions within it took four days.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth's reserves suit each creature's instinctive needs: goats have grass, lions have prey, and each receives fitting sustenance without being forced to adapt against its nature.
rows.anchor: all these reserves found in the earth are in accordance with the instinctive needs of all the creatures

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word suʾāl here means giving people what they instinctively need, as in 14:34.
rows.anchor: The word ﺳﺆلis used in this verse in the same meaning as in:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some readers derive communism from this passage; Islahi says his responsibility is to state its correct interpretation, not separately refute that ideology.
rows.anchor: There is no need to negate the ideology of communism which some people have tried to derive from this section of the verse;

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone can give a person the ability to accept and understand the truth.
rows.anchor: Who else than God has the authority to engender the ability in a person to accept and understand the truth?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression istawā ilā means directing attention or intention toward something.
rows.anchor: means to “to direct attention to that thing;” “to make an intention of that thing.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the earth's earlier stages, God turned His attention to the sky, which was then in cloud form.
rows.anchor: after creating the earth in the afore-mentioned

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky's cloud was dust and vapor, or a nebula; it was still rudimentary, formed during the earth's initial two-day stage, and istawā refers to God's attention to completing it.
rows.anchor: The cloud refers to dust and vapour particles or in scientific terms can be called nebula.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky and earth began to be created at the same time, so the question of which was created first is irrelevant.
rows.anchor: the creation of the sky and the earth began at the same time;

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Like a building, the sky and earth were created through integrated stages, with attention moving between unfinished parts; the analogy helps explain their complex construction.
rows.anchor: similar was the case with bringing into being the sky and the earth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an presents sky and earth together as a building, sometimes mentioning the sky first and sometimes the earth, reflecting the integrated process.
rows.anchor: the Qur’ān has mentioned both of them together in the capacity of a building.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the final stage, God made the rudimentary sky into seven skies and assigned each its laws.
rows.anchor: the Almighty created seven skies from it and subjected it each of them to their laws.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭāʾiʿīn is appropriate only for living beings with intention; Islahi takes the sky and earth's spoken response as evidence of conscious utterance.
rows.anchor: Now this word is only appropriate to be used by those who are living and possess intention.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression's style resembles Solomon's letter to the Queen of Sheba (27:31); Islahi rejects alternative interpretations as failures to recognize this linguistic style.
rows.anchor: is very similar to what Solomon (sws) wrote to the queen of Sheba:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Apparently nonliving things understand God's commands, answer and follow them, and knowingly worship and praise Him; our inability to hear them reflects our limited knowledge.
rows.anchor: the objects of this world which we regard to be non-living and unintelligent understand the directives of their Lord

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural pronoun in fa-qadāhunna and later textual clues show that the sky remained rudimentary and needed completion into seven skies.
rows.anchor: it was in its very rudimentary form and required finishing touches.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God revealed to each sky the duties it would perform in the universe's overall system.
rows.anchor: the Almighty revealed to each of the skies the duties it has in the whole system of this universe.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God adorned the lowest sky with lamps.
rows.anchor: the Almighty decked the lowest sky with lamps.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording shifts from indirect narration to direct address; Islahi notes the eloquence of this shift is explained elsewhere in his exegesis.
rows.anchor: Here the change of style may be kept in consideration.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbal noun ḥifẓan is emphatic; Islahi renders the phrase as God strongly protecting the lowest sky from the devils' incursions.
rows.anchor: The verbal noun وﺣﻔْﻈًﺎ is meant for emphasis.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky's completion took two days, making six days in total for creating sky and earth, as other Qur'anic passages state.
rows.anchor: All these tasks were accomplished in two days, and the sum total of all these days comes out to be six.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhālika summarizes the account: reflecting on the universe shows a wise plan by an all-powerful, all-knowing God.
rows.anchor: The words ذٰﻟﻚ summarize all these details:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universe's wise plan testifies to an all-powerful, all-knowing Creator, whose authority and knowledge extend to every thing, need, and role within it.
rows.anchor: it has been created by the planning of an all-powerful and all-knowing God; it has not come into being accidentally;

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Read with the opening question, the universe testifies that one all-powerful, all-knowing God created and controls it; the question expresses wonder and disgust at people assigning Him partners without justification.
rows.anchor: such is your ignorance that by setting up many hypothetical deities as His partners you are rejecting Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation was gradual, wise, and purposeful, not mere entertainment; its elaborate order entails that a Day of Judgement will come.
rows.anchor: this world has been created very gradually and with great wisdom according to a specific plan.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Creator has immeasurable power and knowledge, needed no help to create, and cannot be helped by anyone.
rows.anchor: neither did He require anyone’s help nor is anyone capable enough to help Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sky and earth are one building occupied by humanity; their harmony shows that the same God created and controls both, disproving separate rulers for roof and floor.
rows.anchor: the sky and the earth are like a building in which God has placed man.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world's comprehensive providence shows that God alone established it and can harm or benefit others, so servants should plead only with Him.
rows.anchor: no one else is capable of setting up such a system; for this reason, His servants should only plead and implore Him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wide system of providence entails a Day of Judgement when people answer for God's favors: the grateful are rewarded and the ungrateful punished.
rows.anchor: those who recognized the obligations they owe to these favours should be rewarded and those who adopted an ungrateful attitude be punished
